text:
mike: Hey team – running a POC with HarborHealth. They flagged a few privacy/security items for the contract review before we move to a staged deploy: SCCs/DPA language, token/log retention, DSAR/deletion process, and whether embeddings are considered customer data. Can someone confirm what we can share for a POC and any quick wording we can provide to legal?

sara: I can take the tech side. For POC we usually offer: short-term logs = 30d default, requestable retention = 0d for session-only mode, KMS-managed keys, and customer namespaces can be deleted on request. Embeddings: stored in customer namespace if using our embeddings endpoint; we can delete that namespace.

mike: Helpful — does "delete namespace" remove embeddings + metadata permanently (and is it auditable)? Customer wants an audit trail for deletions for their compliance team.

sara: Yes — deletion triggers async job and we emit an audit entry to our retention log (read-only) with job id. We can export the audit record as CSV on request. Not currently exposed in the console for POC but ops can run it.

mike: Good to know. devon any legal caveats for the DPA or SCCs? They asked for standard EU SCCs and minor DPA edits.

devon: We can sign the standard EU SCCs as an addendum. For DPA edits: avoid product-level guarantees beyond our policy doc. We provide model of permissible language: "Provider will delete Customer Data upon written request in accordance with the Provider's deletion runbook; Provider will provide an auditable deletion confirmation within 14 days." That's usually acceptable.

mike: Can we give them a short DSAR runbook link and a sample deletion confirmation? They want that in the POC packet tomorrow.

sara: Link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dsar-deletion (internal). Quick sample confirmation text we can use: "Deletion job <JOB_ID> completed on <DATE>. Records removed: namespace cust-harbor-001. Audit ID: <AUDIT_ID>."

mike: Perfect. jess can you own outreach and timeline?

jess: Yep. I'll schedule a 30m sync with HarborHealth for tomorrow 10am PT. I'll ask them if they want us to enable session-only retention for the POC or keep 30d. Also confirm if they need SCCs executed before POC. :calendar:

mike: One more technical ask from their infra folks — they want a curl example to trigger a namespace deletion in the POC. Can we share a sanitized snippet?

sara: Yep, sanitized example below — include in the packet.

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/namespaces/delete \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $POC_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"namespace_id": "cust-harbor-001"}'
```

sara: Note: actual deletes require ops approval for POC accounts — we gate it to prevent accidental wipes. Ops will run the job and return an audit id.

mike: Great. devon any recommended DPA clause for embeddings specifically? They argued embeddings could be re-identifiable and want explicit deletion language.

devon: Add a short clause: "Embeddings and derived artifacts are treated as Customer Data. Provider will delete embeddings on request and will not use them to further train Provider models without Customer's explicit permission." That's our standard stance.

mike: Thanks — that's exactly what they asked for. privacy-bot: Automated note — POC ticket #POC-448 created in Zendesk with due date 2025-06-02.

jess: I'll attach the sample DPA language and the sanitized curl snippet to the ticket and ping HarborHealth legal. Will update here after the sync. :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks everyone — closing loop after the call.
